question: Should experimental `claws update` enter core with one exact `planIntegrity` confirmation that binds capability escalations, or should the CLI itself require a distinct capability-consent acknowledgement before an apply implementation is accepted?
rationale: This is a new core lifecycle and security-boundary contract, not a mechanically verifiable bug fix; the current discussion presents two legitimate UX/security models and the next stacked executor will inherit the decision.

options.title: Approve host-neutral integrity consent
options.body: Keep the planner’s single exact integrity token as the CLI contract while preserving structured escalation records for hosts that render separate consent.

options.title: Require a distinct CLI capability consent
options.body: Define an additional explicit acknowledgement for escalation records before accepting the planner and its future apply path.

options.title: Defer the feature surface
options.body: Keep the stack unmerged until the RFC and lifecycle ownership model receive broader maintainer sponsorship.

recommendation.title: Require a distinct CLI capability consent
recommendation.body: Define an additional explicit acknowledgement for escalation records before accepting the planner and its future apply path.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick-Erichsen is assigned and authored the concrete planner-invariant review threads that this consent decision builds on.
